title: STOMP transformation header reaches unrestricted XStream unmarshalling
reason: CWE-502 is dynamically demonstrated: untrusted STOMP XML reaches unrestricted XStream deserialization and can execute attacker-controlled invocation logic. The harness modifies no ActiveMQ product code; its only addition is a test-only gadget JAR that supplies an observable, non-destructive execution sink.
evidence_summary: The faithful unmodified ActiveMQ 5.11.0 broker accepted an unauthenticated STOMP SEND with transformation:jms-object-xml and no content-length header. The JmsFrameTranslator instantiated XStream and deserialized an attacker-selected dynamic proxy. During TreeSet reconstruction, its compareTo invoked the test-only marker handler loaded solely by the harness classpath, which wrote XSTREAM_STOMP_POC_EXECUTED to the broker-mounted evidence directory. The STOMP client received RECEIPT, while confirmed-marker.txt contains the broker-created marker.

title: Fileserver PUT/MOVE/DELETE allow unauthenticated arbitrary filesystem writes and deletes
reason: The fileserver web.xml leaves RestFilter write-permission-role unset. RestFilter therefore permits unauthenticated PUT, MOVE, and DELETE. Its MOVE handler trusts the Destination HTTP header and copies to new File(destinationUrl.getFile()), allowing an absolute file: URI to select a filesystem path outside the web application.
evidence_summary: The final guest-only run received HTTP 204 for PUT /fileserver/<marker>, HTTP 204 for MOVE with Destination: file:///tmp/csf_64779d6cccce4eb8328ae0c0-arbitrary-write.txt, and confirmed that the exact controlled payload was created at that absolute path outside /opt/activemq/webapps/fileserver. The source file was removed after MOVE. A guest-only DELETE control also returned HTTP 204 and a subsequent GET returned HTTP 404.

title: OpenWire Throwable unmarshalling instantiates attacker-selected classes
reason: Confirmed on a faithful network harness using the exact vulnerable source checkout and its locally built activemq-all-5.15.12.jar. The originally named runtime image had been pruned from Docker, but the immutable exact-revision build directory remained available and was verified by reproduce.sh before execution.
evidence_summary: The executable PoC separately generates a 51-byte attacker OpenWire ExceptionResponse frame naming MarkerThrowable. A real loopback TcpTransport from the immutable ActiveMQ checkout cebbd7fdea0633e6a0cbbef427f9b753949fa531 unmarshals that received frame. Its OpenWire Throwable decoder reflects into the peer-selected public String constructor, which creates evidence/marker.txt containing MARKER_CONSTRUCTOR_INVOKED message=NETWORK_PAYLOAD. The listener also receives org.apache.activemq.command.ExceptionResponse. The EOF recorded afterwards happens only because the one-frame test peer closes its socket after delivery.

title: Default interpolator exposes script execution to template input
reason: The prepared image tag was absent, so validation used the preserved exact Commons Text 1.9 JAR, Commons Lang dependency, compiled endpoint, and endpoint source from the runtime attempt workspace.
evidence_summary: The exact prepared commons-text-1.9.jar evaluates the request payload script:javascript expression. Both the direct harness and copied prepared HTTP endpoint returned before-11.0.32-after, derived by Java.type('java.lang.System').getProperty('java.version').

title: Web Console ships with enabled admin/admin fallback credentials
reason: The target's protected management-console bundles endpoint challenges requests without credentials and with deliberately invalid credentials (both HTTP 401), then grants HTTP 200 access and returns a rendered Apache Felix Web Console response for predictable admin:admin. The runner starts a newly rebuilt image from the supplied runtime Docker context without changing target source, bundles, credentials, or configuration.

evidence_summary.target: Unchanged runtime rebuilt from the supplied attempt Docker context

title: OpenAPI defaults authenticate anonymous callers as the seeded administrator
reason: The runtime configuration has openapi.auth.enabled=false. The executable proof demonstrates an anonymous caller performing state-changing tenant creation that the application attributes to the seeded administrator, while the normal UI route denies the same anonymous caller.
evidence_summary: Against a fresh supplied compose runtime at 127.0.0.1:18195, unauthenticated POST /api/tenant/list returned HTTP 403, while a request with no cookie, Authorization header, secret ID, or secret key to POST /openapi/tenant/save returned HTTP 200 and success=true. An unauthenticated GET /openapi/tenant/get/{generated-name} returned the created tenant with creator=admin and modifier=admin. The PoC then deleted the temporary tenant successfully.
reproduce_command: cd /mnt/dce94ca0-0dcc-412e-b434-f83bb74b35a7/lhq-runtime-v2/poc-agent-critical-findings-20260818T0615Z/poc-workspaces/06-case_020-apache__inlong-CVE-2025-27531-csf_1673a9a5a8937ab9ac0677df && mkdir -p evidence && ./reproduce.sh http://127.0.0.1:18195/inlong/manager | tee evidence/final-run.log

title: Module and package lifecycle APIs allow stored agent shell command execution
reason: The reported security effect requires an unauthorized party to store a lifecycle command that an agent executes. The prepared vulnerable runtime returned HTTP 403 for the complete unauthenticated module-save request. The only successful persistence used the seeded INLONG_ADMIN account, and the compose runtime has no agent-installer service. The faithful source harness confirms the privileged lifecycle execution primitive but does not bridge the denied unauthenticated write boundary. Therefore this reproduction rejects the finding as an externally reachable authorization/RCE vulnerability.

anonymous_module_save.meaning: The lifecycle write endpoint rejects the unauthenticated marker-command request.

authenticated_administrator_write.meaning: The marker command is stored only after a valid administrator session is established.

faithful_agent_execution_harness.meaning: The revision's agent helper executes lifecycle strings through /bin/sh -c, as intended for agent installation operations.

title: Legacy sync RPC accepts unauthenticated superuser data and schema mutations
reason: The supplied vulnerable IoTDB 1.3.3 image accepts unauthenticated legacy-sync handshakes and auto-registers the attacker-chosen database through a superuser session, yielding a schema mutation without an IoTDB login.
evidence_summary: The no-credential Thrift client called legacy handshake with a new database name and received TSStatus code=200. A separately authenticated root/root CLI query then listed root.poc_unauth_case022. Server logs recorded the legacy handshake followed by Execute SetDatabase with TSStatus(code:200).

title: Pipe config transfer lets unauthenticated callers impersonate privileged ConfigNode pipe users
reason: The public DataNode client RPC Pipe endpoint forwarded an unauthenticated ConfigNode Pipe request and executed a privileged database-creation plan. This demonstrates the reported authentication/authorization bypass against the supplied IoTDB 1.3.3 vulnerable runtime.
evidence_summary: Final live run sent a ConfigNode V2 Pipe handshake containing only a foreign cluster ID and timestamp precision; it contained no username/password and opened no IoTDB session. The target returned status_code=200. On the same unauthenticated transport, the harness sent a serialized CreateDatabase ConfigPhysicalPlan for root.unauth_poc and received status_code=200. The target ConfigNode log records successful handshake and ClusterSchemaManager entries for root.unauth_poc.

title: Data-request routes authorize only the claimed team, not the routed dataset or data request
reason: DataRequestRoute authorizes membership for the URL team_id but does not verify that the routed dataset_id or data-request id belongs to that team. This allows a member of one tenant to read and modify another tenant's data request by substituting an authorized team ID in the route.
evidence_summary: Live isolated ChartBrew compose runtime at http://127.0.0.1:34319. The 20260817T230452Z run created separate attacker Team 3 and victim Team 4. Control GET /team/3/datasets/1 returned HTTP 404. With the attacker token, GET /team/3/datasets/1/dataRequests returned HTTP 200 and leaked the victim-only Authorization value. PUT /team/3/datasets/1/dataRequests/1 returned HTTP 200 and changed the request route; victim-authenticated GET confirmed the attacker-controlled route. Raw responses and summary are in runs/20260817T230452Z/.

title: Caller-supplied workflow definitions reach unrestricted Python and JavaScript execution
reason: The vulnerable server image built from the preserved runtime JAR executes caller-supplied INLINE JavaScript with Nashorn Java interoperation enabled; this is the exact capability restricted by the CVE fix's --no-java option.
evidence_summary: POST /api/workflow/test accepted a caller-defined INLINE workflow. The supplied JavaScript invoked Java.type(java.io.File), created /tmp/poc044-cve-2025-26074.marker inside the target container, and returned exists=true plus Java 17.0.19 in a COMPLETED task response. reproduce.sh removes the marker before each request and asserts both the target-container marker and the API response.

title: WS-Security primary signatures are accepted without cryptographic verification
reason: The claimed effect is not dynamically reproducible: a tampered primary WS-Security SignatureValue is rejected before the protected service operation is invoked. The static report location contains commented verification calls, but the executable transport-with-message-credential configuration performed cryptographic rejection through the active runtime path.
evidence_summary: The final reproducible run captured a valid 3,850-byte WS-Security request. Its valid control returned PROTECTED-OPERATION-REACHED:VALID-CONTROL. The PoC then changed only the first Base64 character of the captured ds:SignatureValue and replayed the same SOAP request. The runtime returned HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error with a WS-Security InvalidSecurity fault, and PROTECTED_OPERATION_REACHED=False.

title: Any client:update holder can rotate another client's credential
reason: The vulnerable endpoint authorizes the operation solely with the global client:update scope. A separate attacker OAuth client with that single scope successfully called POST /api/v1/oauth/client/{victim_id}/secret, invalidated the victim credential, and received a usable replacement credential for the victim client.

evidence_summary.cross_client_rotation_response: HTTP 200; returned client_id equaled the separately created victim client id
evidence_summary.secret_handling: Only SHA-256 prefixes of test secrets are persisted; bearer tokens and cleartext secrets are excluded.
